title: Builder
summary: Build complex objects step by step with readable, validated construction.

steps.title: The telescoping constructor
body: var req = new HttpRequestSpec("GET", "/users", null, 30, true, false, null, 3);
What is `30`? `true`? `false`? Constructors with many parameters, especially several of the same type, are unreadable and easy to get wrong in ways the compiler cannot catch.

C# already helps: **named arguments** (`timeoutSeconds: 30`) and **object initialisers** with `init` properties solve most cases. Reach for **Builder** when construction has *steps*, *rules across fields*, or the object should be immutable once built.

steps.prompt: Which option fixes the readability of the call above with the least code?
options: Named arguments or an object initialiser
steps.explain: Builder is not the first tool. Try named arguments and `init` properties first.

steps.title: Builder
body: A **Builder** collects settings through fluent methods, then validates and creates the final object in `Build()`:
public PizzaBuilder Size(int cm) { _size = cm; return this; }
public PizzaBuilder Add(string t) { _toppings.Add(t); return this; }

Each method returns `this`, which is what makes the chain work. `Build` is the one place rules are enforced, so a `Pizza` is always valid. `StringBuilder` and ASP.NET's `WebApplication.CreateBuilder` are builders you have used.

steps.title: Build an email
prompt: Write `record Email(string[] To, string Subject, string Body)` and `class EmailBuilder` with:
- fluent `To(string address)` (can be called several times), `Subject(string s)`, `Body(string b)`
- `Email Build()` that throws `InvalidOperationException` if there is no recipient or no subject; the body defaults to `""`
starter: record Email(string[] To, string Subject, string Body);
solution: record Email(string[] To, string Subject, string Body);
public EmailBuilder To(string address) { _to.Add(address); return this; }
public EmailBuilder Subject(string s) { _subject = s; return this; }
public EmailBuilder Body(string b) { _body = b; return this; }
if (_subject is null) throw new InvalidOperationException("no subject");
